research.vendor: Andreas Gohr and the DokuWiki Community
research.summary: DokuWiki is an open-source wiki engine written in PHP, distributed as date-named stable releases (the release date is the version string) that are followed by lettered hotfix releases. The project publishes its release inventory and download feed, and states in SECURITY.md that only the current stable release is supported; it publishes no version lifecycle table and no API or structured EOL feed.
research.notes: Tier: researched, with ten derived milestones (AGENTS.md rule 8b, disclosed under milestone_provenance). No deterministic source covers DokuWiki: https://endoflife.date/api/all.json lists 477 product slugs (checked 2026-09-23) with no dokuwiki/wiki slug (mediawiki is the only wiki product there) and data/products/ holds no dokuwiki record, so this contribution neither overwrites nor shadows a pipeline. SCOPE AND MODELING: DokuWiki versions ARE their release dates, so the six lines published here are the six stable releases that form the current stable/old-stable/historical chain at the time of research -- 2020-07-29 ("Hogfather"), 2022-07-31 ("Igor"), 2023-04-04 ("Jack Jackrum"), 2024-02-06 ("Kaos"), 2025-05-14 ("Librarian") and 2026-07-14 ("Mort"). Codenames come from the codename the official release tarballs carry in their own VERSION file and the download page prints ('2026-07-14c "Mort"', '2025-05-14b "Librarian"'); they are naming, not lifecycle data. GA (vendor-stated): every stored ga is the vendor's own stable-release date, quoted verbatim from the first-party archive page https://download.dokuwiki.org/archive, which lists each release as '<date> stable release <sha1>'; the same dates are republished in the project's own release feed https://download.dokuwiki.org/rss as 'DokuWiki <date> stable release available'. NOT STATED: DokuWiki publishes no per-version EOL table and states no fixed support duration, so no milestone here is a vendor-stated end date, and eos is null on every line (the project sells nothing and dates no end-of-sale cut-off; a generic support statement is never mapped into eossec or eos). DERIVED eossec/eol (method release-trigger): SECURITY.md states the vendor's support rule -- only the CURRENT stable release is supported, and 'Older versions are not supported, and any vulnerabilities in them will not be fixed.' The dated event that ends a line is therefore the next stable release, whose own published date is the deadline: 2020-07-29 -> 2022-07-31, 2022-07-31 -> 2023-04-04, 2023-04-04 -> 2024-02-06, 2024-02-06 -> 2025-05-14, 2025-05-14 -> 2026-07-14. Both eossec and eol carry the same derived deadline because the vendor's own sentence ends bug and security support together ('not supported' and 'will not be fixed'). Each derived value is published only through milestone_provenance with its base date, its trigger release and the exact vendor quote, is labeled derived in every presentation, and is excluded from the exact-day Atom/RSS/iCalendar feeds and the OpenEoX export (engine/derived.py, engine/feeds.py, engine/openeox.py). RULE HISTORY (the rule is the vendor's long-standing policy, not a new one): SECURITY.md was created 2021-12-12 (commit 22b04d8db65da89d8f091b893e86c3c3b1568ffb) stating 'Security vulnerabilities can be reported for the current stable release (branch `stable`) and the `master` branch.' and promising that a fix for a current-stable issue is either a hotfix or the next proper release -- substantively the same current-stable-only rule. The wording was strengthened on 2026-07-20 (commit e014d4c892e4ef0acfe31bae0274dc38e5366089) to the sentence quoted above. The earliest derived trigger used here is 2022-07-31, which falls after 2021-12-12, so every derived transition is covered by the rule as it stood at its own trigger date; both revisions are cited verbatim in the evidence. SECURITY.md never stated a fixed support duration in any revision, so nothing here is duration-derived. HOTFIXES ARE NOT TRIGGERS: each stable line is followed by lettered hotfix releases (2020-07-29a, 2022-07-31a/b, 2023-04-04a/b, 2024-02-06a/b, 2025-05-14a/b, 2026-07-14a/b/c); a hotfix does not supersede a line as the current stable release, so no hotfix publication date is used as a milestone here. The download page currently offers 2026-07-14c as 'Stable' and 2025-05-14b as 'Old Stable'; those are download-channel labels, not deadlines. DISCLOSED CONTRADICTION (a derived deadline is the vendor's POLICY deadline, not an observed last patch): the project has in fact backported security hotfixes onto lines that had already stopped being the current stable release, so a line's derived eossec/eol can precede its last shipped security patch. Verified instances: 2020-07-29's hotfix a was published 2022-09-04, after the 2022-07-31 stable release had ended that line; 2022-07-31's hotfix b was published 2023-05-16, after the 2023-04-04 stable release had ended that line; and 2023-04-04's hotfix b was published 2024-08-05, after the 2024-02-06 stable release had ended that line. These are security fixes, not routine patches (the 2020-07-29a release object is titled 'SECURITY HOTFIX for XSS vulnerability #3761'; the 2023-04-04b commit series fixes a stored XSS). They are disclosed rather than hidden and are not used as support evidence: the record states the deadline the vendor's published rule produces, and a discretionary backport after that deadline does not extend it. All three counterexample feed dates are quoted verbatim in the evidence. CURRENT LINE UNKNOWN: 2026-07-14 is the current stable release, so the vendor's rule ends nothing yet and its eos/eossec/eol are null; no date is projected from the cadence between the stable releases above (the gaps vary from about 8 to 24 months), and absence stays absent. SOURCE LIMITS: (1) https://www.dokuwiki.org/* returns HTTP 402 (Payment Required) to this research client, so the wiki's own release/changes/support pages could not be read; the first-party download site (download.dokuwiki.org, HTTP 200), its release feed, and SECURITY.md in the vendor's own repository were used instead; (2) release candidates (2020-06-01, 2020-06-09, 2022-06-26) and the pre-2020 stable releases the archive page lists are outside the researched window and are not published here; (3) one hotfix has no Git tag at all (release-2023-04-04b; release-2024-02-06b and the others are tagged) -- for it the archive page and the project's own RSS feed are the durable first-party record and are the sources used; (4) GitHub release metadata was used only to cross-check that each stable release's tag publication day agrees with the archive page, which it does for all six lines. If a deterministic collector for DokuWiki is ever added, this researched record must be retired in favour of it (rule 8).
